# LLM Provider Flexibility

Dimension 3 of 7 for [Goose AI Agent](../citations.md) research.

## Provider Support

Goose supports LLM providers across five categories [3]:

### Standard API Providers

| Provider | Auth | Special Features | Limitations |
|----------|------|------------------|-------------|
| Anthropic | API key | Auto prompt caching | Claude 4 works best [3] |
| OpenAI | API key | Custom endpoint for vLLM/KServe | o1-mini/o1-preview unsupported (no tool calling) [3] |
| Google Gemini | API key | Configurable thinking levels, free tier | — |
| Mistral AI | API key | Codestral, Pixtral models | — |
| xAI | API key | Grok-3, 131,072 context | — |
| Groq | API key | Free tier, kimi-k2-instruct | — |

### Cloud/Enterprise Providers

Amazon Bedrock (AWS credentials, Claude prompt caching), Azure OpenAI (API key or credential chain), GCP Vertex AI (service account, org policy filtering), Databricks (token, prompt caching), Snowflake Cortex (PAT), VMware Tanzu (API key, dynamic model fetching), OVHcloud AI [3].

### API Gateways

OpenRouter (200+ models), LiteLLM (unified proxy, auto prompt caching), Tetrate Agent Router (PKCE auth, model failover), Avian (DeepSeek, Kimi), Novita AI (90+ models), Venice AI (privacy-focused) [3].

### Local/Self-Hosted

Ollama (auto-detects models, no auth), Ollama Cloud, LM Studio (localhost:1234), Docker Model Runner (free, OpenAI-compatible), Ramalama (OCI container runtimes) [3].

### ACP Providers

Claude ACP (uses existing Claude Code subscription), ChatGPT Codex ACP (uses existing ChatGPT subscription), Cursor Agent, Amp ACP, Pi ACP [9].

## Provider Count

Source claims vary: goose-docs.ai homepage says "15+" [3], other sources cite "25+" [34], and one analysis claims "40+" [3]. The variation likely reflects growth over time and counting methodology (some include ACP providers, some don't).

## Tool Calling Requirement

Goose "relies heavily on tool calling capabilities" — this is a hard requirement for autonomous operation [3]. Models without tool calling (e.g., o1-mini, o1-preview, DeepSeek-R1 native) must disable all extensions and operate in basic chat mode [3].

Best-performing models for tool calling are Claude 4 series (Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5) — "currently works best" per documentation [3].

## Prompt Caching

Automatic prompt caching is enabled for Anthropic models via Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Databricks, OpenRouter, and LiteLLM providers [3]. This reduces costs by caching frequently-used context.

## Multi-Model Configuration

Planning mode allows dedicated planner models separate from execution models [3]. Subagents can use different models than the main session, configurable ad-hoc [40].

## ACP (Agent Client Protocol)

ACP is a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol for client-to-agent communication [9][51]. It enables use of existing subscriptions (Claude Code, ChatGPT Plus/Pro) without separate per-token API costs [9]. Originally created by the Zed editor team [51]. Goose is adopting ACP as "primary interface for all goose clients — desktop, CLI, and beyond" [51].

**Important disambiguation:** ACP (Agent Client Protocol) is distinct from "Agentic Commerce Protocol" (OpenAI + Stripe for e-commerce transactions at agenticcommerce.dev) [3].

## Counter-Perspectives

### Tool Calling Failures

Open-source models struggle significantly with tool calling even when they have technical capability [47]. Mixtral has a 10% failure rate on tool calls due to JSON formatting issues [66]. Quantized models refuse to discover or call tools properly [62]. OpenAI rarely produces malformed calls, Anthropic excels at chaining, but open-source models show inconsistent parameter handling [63].

### Model Quality Degradation

Performance degrades dramatically with smaller models [29]. 7B parameter models show "noticeable degradation on multi-file refactoring tasks" [29]. Llama 3 70B requires 48GB+ RAM; smaller models fit modest hardware but produce lower quality [27][29]. Llama 4 via Ollama shows ~20% higher error rate on complex tool chains [25].

### Context Window Problems

Ollama defaults to 2048 tokens while Goose's system prompt alone is ~1k tokens, causing silent truncation [46]. Hard-coded context lengths default to 32k for non-standard model names [46]. Token counting shows 4x discrepancies between UI and actual usage [45].

### Compound Reliability

Multi-step reliability degrades multiplicatively: a model 90% reliable per step is only 59% reliable across 5 steps [59]. This makes long-running workflows (10-30 minutes, dozens of steps) increasingly fragile [59].

### Cost Reality

With cloud models, Goose costs $5-20/month for moderate usage, making the cost advantage over Claude Code ($20/month) "modest to nonexistent" [27]. The $0 local option requires $4,000+ hardware investment (est.) [27].

## Gaps and Limitations

- No official benchmarks comparing provider performance within Goose
- ACP adoption timeline (4-phase, Feb-Apr 2026) status unclear [51]
- Provider failover/redundancy not documented
- No usage data on local vs cloud model adoption split
